natural_language_question: For Central-region accounts, compare engagement in the previous quarter with the quarter before it.
reference_sql:
WITH q AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN i.interaction_at >= DATE '2026-01-01' AND i.interaction_at < DATE '2026-04-01' THEN i.engagement_points ELSE 0 END) AS prev_q,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i.interaction_at >= DATE '2026-04-01' AND i.interaction_at < DATE '2026-07-01' THEN i.engagement_points ELSE 0 END) AS this_q
  FROM interactions i
  INNER JOIN contacts c ON i.contact_id = c.contact_id
  INNER JOIN accounts a ON c.account_id = a.account_id
  WHERE a.region = 'Central'
)
SELECT
  prev_q AS prev_quarter_points,
  this_q AS this_quarter_points,
  this_q - prev_q AS absolute_change,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN prev_q = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (this_q - prev_q) / CAST(prev_q AS DOUBLE) * 100 END, 2) AS pct_change,
  CASE WHEN this_q > prev_q THEN 'up' WHEN this_q < prev_q THEN 'down' ELSE 'flat' END AS direction
FROM q;
reference_fields: interactions.contact_id, interactions.interaction_at, interactions.engagement_points, contacts.contact_id, contacts.account_id, accounts.account_id, accounts.region
judge_reference: Total engagement_points for Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 for the named region, the absolute and percentage change, and the direction. Q1 and Q2 are the two most recent complete calendar quarters relative to the reference date 2026-08-01.
derivation_rationale: Q1 2026 = 2026-01-01..2026-04-01, Q2 2026 = 2026-04-01..2026-07-01 - the two most recent COMPLETE quarters (data ends 2026-07-28, so Q3 is excluded). INNER JOIN interactions -> contacts -> accounts, filter to the region, SUM(engagement_points) per window, then compute absolute and percentage change and direction.

natural_language_question: Among Central-region accounts, which three campaign types generated the most customer activity?
reference_sql:
SELECT ca.campaign_type AS entity, SUM(i.engagement_points) AS metric
FROM campaigns ca
INNER JOIN interactions i ON ca.campaign_id = i.campaign_id
INNER JOIN contacts c ON i.contact_id = c.contact_id
INNER JOIN accounts a ON c.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.region = 'Central'
GROUP BY ca.campaign_type ORDER BY metric DESC, entity ASC LIMIT 3;
reference_fields: campaigns.campaign_id, campaigns.campaign_type, interactions.campaign_id, interactions.contact_id, interactions.engagement_points, contacts.contact_id, contacts.account_id, accounts.account_id, accounts.region

derivation_rationale: Join campaigns -> interactions -> contacts -> accounts, filter to the region, SUM(engagement_points) per campaign_type, order desc with campaign_type tie-break, top 3.

natural_language_question: Right now, which accounts are carrying the biggest unresolved queue of access support cases?
expected_answer: Reynolds Williams and Williams | 3; Barnett Brown | 2; Gordon Rivers and Arnold | 2; Hansen LLC | 2; Hodges Group | 2
reference_sql:
SELECT a.account_name AS entity, COUNT(s.case_id) AS metric
FROM accounts a INNER JOIN support_cases s ON a.account_id = s.account_id
WHERE s.category = 'Access'
  AND s.status IN ('New', 'InProgress', 'PendingCustomer')
GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name ORDER BY metric DESC, entity ASC LIMIT 5;

natural_language_question: Looking at preferred-tier accounts, which region's engagement held up best between the January-March and April-June 2026 periods?
reference_sql:
WITH by_region AS (
  SELECT a.region,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i.interaction_at >= DATE '2026-01-01' AND i.interaction_at < DATE '2026-04-01' THEN i.engagement_points ELSE 0 END) AS prev_q,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i.interaction_at >= DATE '2026-04-01' AND i.interaction_at < DATE '2026-07-01' THEN i.engagement_points ELSE 0 END) AS this_q
  FROM accounts a
  INNER JOIN contacts c ON a.account_id = c.account_id
  INNER JOIN interactions i ON c.contact_id = i.contact_id
  WHERE a.region IS NOT NULL AND a.customer_tier = 'Preferred'
  GROUP BY a.region
)
SELECT region AS entity, prev_q AS prev_quarter_points, this_q AS this_quarter_points,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN prev_q = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (this_q - prev_q) / CAST(prev_q AS DOUBLE) * 100 END, 2) AS pct_change
FROM by_region ORDER BY pct_change DESC NULLS LAST, region ASC LIMIT 1;
reference_fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.region, accounts.customer_tier, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, interactions.contact_id, interactions.engagement_points, interactions.interaction_at
judge_reference: The single region with the highest percentage change in engagement_points from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026 among accounts in the named customer tier - the largest gain, or (if every region declined) the smallest decline. Regions with zero Q1 engagement are excluded.
derivation_rationale: Q1 2026 = 2026-01-01..2026-04-01, Q2 2026 = 2026-04-01..2026-07-01 (the two most recent COMPLETE quarters; data ends 2026-07-28). INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> interactions, restrict to the tier, SUM(engagement_points) per region per window. pct_change = (Q2 - Q1) / Q1 * 100. Regions with zero Q1 are undefined and sorted last. Take the region with the highest pct_change (does NOT assume growth).

natural_language_question: For education-industry accounts, what share of support cases met the SLA deadline?
reference_sql:
SELECT ROUND(
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND s.resolved_at <= s.sla_due_at)
  * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS sla_compliance_pct
FROM support_cases s INNER JOIN accounts a ON s.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.industry = 'Education';
judge_reference: A single percentage (0-100, two decimals): of all support cases for accounts in the named industry, the share resolved on or before their SLA deadline. Unresolved cases count against the rate.
derivation_rationale: INNER JOIN support_cases to accounts on account_id, filter to the industry. A case is within SLA when resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_at <= sla_due_at. Rate = 100.0 * within-SLA count / total case count, rounded to 2 places.

natural_language_question: Among education-industry accounts, which ones have a large unresolved case backlog and no engagement in the last 60 days?
expected_answer: Hansen LLC | 7 | 0; Jones PLC | 6 | 0; Lynn PLC | 6 | 0; Smith and Sons | 6 | 0; Blankenship Alexander | 5 | 0
reference_sql:
WITH open_cases AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS open_case_count FROM support_cases
  WHERE status IN ('New', 'InProgress', 'PendingCustomer') GROUP BY account_id
), recent_engagement AS (
  SELECT c.account_id, COUNT(*) AS recent_interaction_count
  FROM interactions i INNER JOIN contacts c ON i.contact_id = c.contact_id
  WHERE i.interaction_at >= DATE '2026-06-02' AND c.account_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.account_id
)
SELECT a.account_name AS entity,
       COALESCE(oc.open_case_count, 0) AS open_case_count,
       COALESCE(re.recent_interaction_count, 0) AS recent_interaction_count
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN open_cases oc ON a.account_id = oc.account_id
LEFT JOIN recent_engagement re ON a.account_id = re.account_id
WHERE a.industry = 'Education'
  AND COALESCE(oc.open_case_count, 0) >= 3
  AND COALESCE(re.recent_interaction_count, 0) = 0
ORDER BY open_case_count DESC, entity ASC LIMIT 5;
reference_fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.account_name, accounts.industry, support_cases.account_id, support_cases.status, interactions.contact_id, interactions.interaction_at, contacts.contact_id, contacts.account_id
judge_reference: Accounts in the named industry with at least three unresolved support cases and zero interactions (via their contacts) in the 60 days before the reference date, with the two supporting numbers.
derivation_rationale: Count unresolved cases per account and interactions since 2026-06-02 (60 days before reference_today 2026-08-01) attributed through the contact's account. Filter to the industry, >= 3 open cases, 0 recent interactions, order by open-case count desc with account_name tie-break, top 5.

natural_language_question: For awareness campaigns, rank contact titles by their total multi-touch attribution weight.
expected_answer: Business Analyst | 8.9691; Procurement Manager | 8.9451; Operations Director | 7.2499; IT Director | 5.3333; Program Manager | 4.3167; Service Delivery Manager | 2.8334; Customer Success Manager | 2.6999
reference_sql:
SELECT c.title AS entity,
       ROUND(SUM(cc.attribution_weight), 4) AS total_attribution_weight
FROM contacts c
INNER JOIN contact_campaigns cc ON c.contact_id = cc.contact_id
INNER JOIN campaigns ca ON cc.campaign_id = ca.campaign_id
WHERE ca.campaign_type = 'Awareness'
  AND c.title IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.title
ORDER BY total_attribution_weight DESC, entity ASC;
reference_fields: contacts.contact_id, contacts.title, contact_campaigns.contact_id, contact_campaigns.campaign_id, contact_campaigns.attribution_weight, campaigns.campaign_id, campaigns.campaign_type
judge_reference: Contact titles ranked by summed attribution_weight for memberships of campaigns of the named type, four decimals, highest first. Memberships whose attribution_weight is missing contribute nothing.
derivation_rationale: INNER JOIN contacts -> contact_campaigns -> campaigns (all three essential: contacts supplies the grouping title, contact_campaigns the weight, campaigns the filter). Filter to the campaign_type, GROUP BY contacts.title, ROUND(SUM(contact_campaigns.attribution_weight), 4). Rows with a NULL attribution_weight (the ~2.5% missing-value imperfection) are skipped by SUM - the declared NULL handling for this measure. Order desc with title tie-break.
